messages:
maya: Quick heads up — on the prod-long-session run I saw steady KV memory growth over ~3h, not matching request volume. dump + small heap profile attached.

jamal: Can you paste the metric spikes? kv_mem_total / kv_residency_pct?

maya: Sure. Quick prometheus queries I ran:
```
max_over_time(kv_mem_bytes[3h])
rate(kv_eviction_count[5m])
kv_residency_percent{pool="main"}
``` 
Results: mem up ~22% over baseline, residency stable ~88%, eviction_count increased but low rate (spiky). frag_ratio metric drifting upward.

liam: Interesting — residency steady but frag ratio up implies fragmentation not eviction. Any long sequences or long-context tests running? Could be KV pages not coalescing.

maya: Long-chat-run with sequences up to 150k tokens (simulated). Also saw periodic small GC-ish pauses in the runtime logs around 12:23 and 12:57.

anya: Can you share a sample of the eviction log lines? format changed recently after the paging refactor.

maya: pasted log snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T12:23:11Z] kvpager: evict candidate: shard=7, reason=low_usage, size=6.4MB, age=2h14m
[2026-03-12T12:23:11Z] kvpager: fragmented=0.31, free_slots=124
[2026-03-12T12:57:03Z] kvpager: compaction-scan started shard=3
```

teo: Fragmentation 0.31 is notable. Our compaction currently runs opportunistically; with long contexts it may never trigger enough. Suggest adding a compaction pressure metric and an eviction_age_hist so we can see how old evicted entries are.

jamal: Agreed. For observability: add these panels to the per-pool dashboard: kv_mem_bytes (timeline), kv_mem_growth_rate (delta over 1h), kv_residency_percent, kv_frag_ratio, eviction_count_by_age_bucket.

liam: Also instrument sample-based residency per-request-id to detect hotset drift. Current residency only shows pool-level average which hides multi-modal distributions.

maya: I'll attach the heap diff and profile. Also reran with kernel-selection toggled off for these runs; no sig change, so likely runtime allocation pattern not kernel related.

anya: Could be a change in batching heuristic leading to more long-lived KV handles. Any recent PRs to continuous batching or handle lifetimes?

teo: I have a small draft change to lower KV handle TTL from 30m -> 10m when session inactive; if fragmentation is the cause that may help. But need metrics to validate.

maya: For validation plan:
- add eviction_age_hist and frag_ratio panel
- add eviction_reasons_breakdown (low_usage vs force) as counters
- enable residency sampling with p=0.05 and tag by route
- run long-session job with and w/o TTL change and compare

jamal: +1. Also add an alert: if kv_mem_growth_rate > 10%/h AND frag_ratio > 0.25 for 1h, page eng-runtime :pager_duty:

infra-bot: alert rule created (rule_id=kv_frag_growth_1767). Will start evaluating in 5m. :gear:

liam: One more ask — capture per-kernel memory allocs in the profile (to rule out allocator regressions). I'll sync with infra to ensure jemalloc stats are exposed.

maya: OK I'll implement dashboards and run an A/B. Posting results in this thread when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:

teo: :eyes: keep an eye on compaction latency when you lower TTL — compaction runs could add latency.

maya: noted. will throttle compaction to background low-priority during the test.
